# Bike repair stand placement — 2026-10-09

**Participants:** Anouk Brennagh (Parks Officer), Sami Okonkwo-Hart (Cycling Club)

Anouk: "The public repair stand goes by the river path entrance, not in the car park. The river path is where the flats happen."

Sami: "Put the pump on a chain; the last one walked off in a week."

The map and coverage showed only two active positions (ferry late sailings and winter rota hours at the tool library), and the focus returned no witness-depth match. None overlap the bike stand subject, so I did not drill into them further. Anouk Brennagh and Sami Okonkwo-Hart are not in the roster, so I did not expand their actor nodes. The perspective holds no position on cycling or bike-stand placement.

positions.name: RepairStandSiteAndPumpSecurity
positions.frame: Where should the public bike repair stand go, and what does it take to keep its equipment in place, given where riders actually break down and where kit has gone missing before?
positions.why: Both statements read the same public repair-stand installation from the standpoint of evidence about use and loss. Anouk places the stand where the flats happen, at the river path entrance and not the car park. Sami asks for the pump to be chained because the last one walked off in a week. One argues from where need arises and the other from where theft arises, so both treat the stand's design as following observed local behaviour. The set holds no real tension, though the siting and the securing are separate decisions. Nothing in the graph covers this topic, so the position stands alone with no existing structure to attach to.

placements.title: Public cycling kit goes where riders break down and is secured where kit goes missing
placements.frame: Where does the evidence of actual rider need or past loss say this public cycling facility, or its equipment, should be placed or protected?
placements.why: Nothing in the graph covers public cycling infrastructure. The position pairs two statements, both arguing that the repair stand's siting and security should follow observed local behaviour: where the flats happen, and where the last pump was stolen. This is a subject future envelopes about public facilities could keep feeding, not a one-time fact. The graph's two existing leaves, ferry sailings and tool-library hours, are structurally similar in shape but concern other subjects, so reusing either would be word-shape overlap only. It stands alone as a new region.
